title: regex_replace() silently returns the unmodified source on an invalid pattern — sanitization/redaction steps can no-op with zero signal
existing_state: RegexReplace catches both RegexMatchTimeoutException and ArgumentException (invalid pattern) and returns the original source string unchanged (Services/Scripting/Functions/StringFunctions.cs:165-176). A script using regex_replace to strip secrets, ANSI codes, or sensitive fields from device output before logging/notifying — the docs themselves recommend a regex_replace incantation for ANSI stripping — gets the raw, unsanitized text back if the pattern has a typo or a variable-built pattern is malformed, with no error, no warning, nothing in output. regex_match has the related problem that an invalid pattern and a legitimate no-match are both "" (StringFunctions.cs:194-208), so a script cannot tell 'pattern broken' from 'value absent'.
recommendation: Distinguish the two failure modes in StringFunctions: an ArgumentException (user wrote a bad pattern — deterministic, will fail on every host) should fail the step or at minimum set _last_error and emit a warning; a RegexMatchTimeoutException can keep the soft fallback but should still warn. Apply the same treatment to regex_match/regex_match_all/regex_groups, which currently swallow ArgumentException into empty results (StringFunctions.cs:224-225, 248-249).
user_benefit: When a redaction or extraction pattern is broken, the owner finds out immediately instead of discovering unsanitized output in logs/notifications, or extraction silently yielding empty values across an entire fleet run.

evidence.note: catch (ArgumentException) { return source; } — invalid pattern returns input unchanged
regex_match: invalid pattern and no-match both return ""
regex_match_all/regex_groups swallow ArgumentException into empty lists
